name: Thalamic reticular nucleus (TRN) GABAergic neuron
anatomy_mentioned: thin shell/sheet wrapping the anterior and lateral surfaces of the dorsal thalamus, with dorsal and ventral extensions
between the external medullary lamina and the internal capsule
morphology_summary: Neurons of a thin lamellar shell traversed by thalamocortical and corticothalamic fibres; thin axons with intrareticular collaterals and diffuse branches across relay nuclei (e.g. VP and posterior thalamus); presynaptic dendrites; no direct cortical projection. nRT-thalamic terminals mostly form single synapses on thin distal relay-cell dendrites (F terminals in dLGN). Core/inner cells reported to have larger somata and more extensive dendrites than edge cells.
ephys_summary: Fast-spiking with low-threshold Ca2+ spike-driven repetitive bursts at spindle frequency (spindle pacemaker in NREM sleep); tonic firing in wakefulness (visual TRN in monkey: ~45 spikes/s background, strong fast transient visual responses, attention-modulated). No tonic GABA-A current (lacks alpha4/delta subunits); mutual GABA-A (occasionally GABA-B) inhibition between TRN cells; connexin36-dependent gap-junction-coupled clusters; group I mGluR depolarization vs group II mGluR hyperpolarization; presynaptic 5-HT1A/5-HT2A and adenosine A1 modulation of GABA release.
subtypes_noted: Report treats TRN GABAergic neurons as one class with layered heterogeneity: (i) major transcriptomic gradient with mutually exclusive Spp1+ (core, burst-prone, first-order-projecting) and Ecel1+ (shell, low-burst, higher-order-projecting) poles (Li et al., 2020; Hartley et al., 2024) -- proposed below as separate subtype nodes; (ii) PV+ (rhythmogenic, first-order-projecting, ~70% of TRN cells) vs SOM+ (limbic, higher-order-projecting) populations (Clemente-Perez et al., 2017; Inserra et al., 2021; Flores et al., 2026; Klimczak et al., 2024), with SOM->PV intra-TRN inhibition (Cho et al., 2025); (iii) sector-defined limbic vs sensory subnetworks (Halassa et al., 2014); (iv) input-convergent (~25%) vs single-source neurons in somatosensory TRN tiers (Lam et al., 2011); (v) two gap-junction cluster types (within-module vs across-thickness) (Lee et al., 2014). Note: cat/monkey work reports somatostatin-like immunoreactivity in most TRN neurons (Graybiel et al., 1983).

name: TRN Spp1+ core GABAergic neuron
anatomy_mentioned: central core (inner region) of the thalamic reticular nucleus
morphology_summary: Core/inner TRN neurons with larger somata and more extensive dendritic trees than edge neurons (review summary, Flores et al., 2026); core-like anatomical structure.
ephys_summary: High bursting activity; projects preferentially to first-order thalamic nuclei; contributes to sleep spindle generation and delta power during slow-wave sleep.
subtypes_noted: Pole of a continuous transcriptomic gradient rather than a discrete cluster (Li et al., 2020); intermediate cells lie between Spp1 and Ecel1 poles. Overlap with PV+ rhythmogenic, first-order-projecting population (Clemente-Perez et al., 2017) is plausible but not stated explicitly in the report.

name: TRN Ecel1+ shell (edge) GABAergic neuron
anatomy_mentioned: bordering shell (edge) of the thalamic reticular nucleus
morphology_summary: Shell-like/edge anatomical organization at TRN borders; smaller somata and less extensive dendrites than core neurons (by contrast in Flores et al., 2026).
ephys_summary: Low bursting activity relative to Spp1+ neurons; projects preferentially to higher-order thalamic nuclei; antagonizes sleep spindle duration.
subtypes_noted: Pole of a continuous transcriptomic gradient (Li et al., 2020). Possible correspondence with SOM+ limbic/higher-order-projecting TRN population (Clemente-Perez et al., 2017) is not stated explicitly in the report.
